page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-32GB is a Cloud Native virtual machine running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, and the system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding 2.67 GB of memory per core. Local storage is not bundled with this instance type, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is in the bottom 10%, reflecting the shared CPU allocation and modest clock speed. However, multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the middle 50% average. Memory bandwidth tests for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks show average performance, though the PassMark memory score is weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Static web serving throughput and Redis SET operations both perform at average levels.

The shared CPU model offers a cost-effective resource density for multi-threaded workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated single-core performance. While it is poorly suited for heavy single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM text generation, its average multi-core capabilities make it a viable option for horizontal web serving, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and moderate database operations.
